questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I am busy.”
options: He said that he was busy.
He said that he is busy.
He said that I was busy.
He said that he had been busy.
questions.explanation: Rule: reporting verb in past, so present tense shifts back (am becomes was) and 'I' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, “I like mangoes.”
options: She said that she likes mangoes.
She said that she liked mangoes.
She said that I liked mangoes.
She said that she had liked mangoes.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present backshifts to simple past; 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Ravi said to me, “I will help you.”
options: Ravi told me that I would help him.
Ravi told me that he will help me.
Ravi told me that he would help me.
Ravi told me that he would help him.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'said to' becomes 'told'; will becomes would; 'I' becomes 'he' (the speaker) and 'you' becomes 'me' (the listener).
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Mother said, “I have cooked dinner.”
options: Mother said that she has cooked dinner.
Mother said that I had cooked dinner.
Mother said that she would cook dinner.
Mother said that she had cooked dinner.
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect becomes past perfect; 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Kumar said, “I wrote a poem.”
options: Kumar said that he had written a poem.
Kumar said that he wrote a poem.
Kumar said that he has written a poem.
Kumar said that I had written a poem.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past backshifts to past perfect; 'I' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said, “The earth moves round the sun.”
options: The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth would move round the sun.
questions.explanation: Rule: a universal truth keeps its present tense even after a past reporting verb.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I can swim.”
options: He said that he can swim.
He said that I could swim.
He said that he could swim.
He said that he would swim.
questions.explanation: Rule: can becomes could; 'I' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said to him, “You are late.”
options: She told him that she was late.
She told him that he is late.
She told him that he had been late.
She told him that he was late.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'said to' becomes 'told'; 'you' becomes 'him' (the listener); are becomes was.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: They said, “We are playing cricket.”
options: They said that they were playing cricket.
They said that they are playing cricket.
They said that we were playing cricket.
They said that they had been playing cricket.
questions.explanation: Rule: present continuous backshifts to past continuous; 'we' becomes 'they'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Anita said, “I may go to Madurai.”
options: Anita said that she may go to Madurai.
Anita said that she might go to Madurai.
Anita said that she could go to Madurai.
Anita said that I might go to Madurai.
questions.explanation: Rule: may becomes might; 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said to me, “Where do you live?”
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where he lived.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me that where I lived.
questions.explanation: Rule: a wh-question becomes a statement-order clause (no auxiliary 'do'); present backshifts to past; 'you' becomes 'I' (me, the listener).
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said to him, “Are you coming?”
options: She asked him that he was coming.
She asked him if was he coming.
She asked him if he is coming.
She asked him if he was coming.
questions.explanation: Rule: a yes/no question uses 'if/whether' with statement word order; present continuous becomes past continuous.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said to the students, “Open your books.”
options: The teacher ordered the students to open their books.
The teacher ordered the students that they open their books.
The teacher ordered the students to open your books.
The teacher asked the students if they opened their books.
questions.explanation: Rule: an imperative uses a verb like ordered/told plus 'to' + V1; 'your' becomes 'their'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The doctor said to the patient, “Do not eat oily food.”
options: The doctor advised the patient to not eating oily food.
The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.
The doctor advised the patient that he did not eat oily food.
The doctor advised the patient do not eat oily food.
questions.explanation: Rule: a negative imperative becomes 'not to + V1' after advised/told.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Ravi said, “Hurrah! We have won the match.”
options: Ravi exclaimed with joy that we have won the match.
Ravi exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
Ravi exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
Ravi exclaimed with joy that they would win the match.
questions.explanation: Rule: exclamation words (Hurrah) become 'exclaimed with joy'; present perfect becomes past perfect; 'we' becomes 'they'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, “Alas! I have lost my purse.”
options: She exclaimed with joy that she had lost her purse.
She exclaimed with sorrow that I had lost my purse.
She exclaimed with sorrow that she has lost her purse.
She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Alas' becomes 'exclaimed with sorrow'; present perfect becomes past perfect; 'I/my' become 'she/her'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Arun said to Babu, “Will you lend me your pen?”
options: Arun asked Babu if he would lend him his pen.
Arun asked Babu if he will lend him his pen.
Arun asked Babu would he lend him his pen.
Arun asked Babu if I would lend you my pen.
questions.explanation: Rule: a yes/no question uses 'if'; will becomes would; pronouns follow the speaker and listener (me becomes him, your becomes his).
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I have been waiting since morning.”
options: He said that he has been waiting since morning.
He said that he had been waiting since morning.
He said that he was waiting since morning.
He said that I had been waiting since morning.
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect continuous becomes past perfect continuous.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I met her yesterday.”
options: He said that he met her yesterday.
He said that he had met her the next day.
He said that he had met her the previous day.
He said that he has met her the previous day.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, “I will come tomorrow.”
options: She said that she will come tomorrow.
She said that she would come the previous day.
She said that she would have come the next day.
She said that she would come the next day.
questions.explanation: Rule: will becomes would; 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I am leaving today.”
options: He said that he was leaving that day.
He said that he was leaving today.
He said that he is leaving that day.
He said that he had left that day.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'today' becomes 'that day'; present continuous becomes past continuous.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: “I saw him here last night,” said Meera.
options: Meera said that she saw him here last night.
Meera said that she had seen him there the previous night.
Meera said that she had seen him here the previous night.
Meera said that I had seen him there the previous night.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past becomes past perfect; 'here' becomes 'there'; 'last night' becomes 'the previous night'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Rohit said to Mani, “Why are you crying?”
options: Rohit asked Mani why was he crying.
Rohit asked Mani why you were crying.
Rohit asked Mani why he was crying.
Rohit asked Mani why he is crying.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question keeps its question word but takes statement word order; present continuous becomes past continuous; 'you' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, “What a beautiful garden this is!”
options: She exclaimed that this is a very beautiful garden.
She asked what a beautiful garden it was.
She exclaimed that it is a very beautiful garden.
She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful garden.
questions.explanation: Rule: an exclamation becomes a statement with 'exclaimed that'; 'What a' becomes 'a very'; 'this' becomes 'it' and is becomes was.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The manager said to the clerk, “Please send the file.”
options: The manager requested the clerk to send the file.
The manager ordered the clerk to send the file please.
The manager requested the clerk that he sends the file.
The manager asked the clerk if he sent the file.
questions.explanation: Rule: an imperative with 'please' becomes 'requested ... to + V1'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Father said to me, “You must study hard.”
options: Father told me that he must study hard.
Father told me that I must study hard.
Father told me that you must study hard.
Father told me that I had must study hard.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'must' stays unchanged in reported speech; 'you' becomes 'I' (the listener, me).

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: “Don't make noise,” said the teacher to the boys.
options: The teacher forbade the boys to made noise.
The teacher forbade the boys that they do not make noise.
The teacher forbade the boys to make noise.
The teacher asked the boys if they made noise.
questions.explanation: Rule: a negative command can be reported with 'forbade ... to + V1' (or 'told ... not to').
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The captain said to the players, “Let us win this match.”
options: The captain proposed to the players that we should win this match.
The captain proposed to the players that they will win that match.
The captain asked the players to let them win that match.
The captain proposed to the players that they should win that match.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Let us' (suggestion) becomes 'proposed that ... should'; 'us' becomes 'they'; 'this' becomes 'that'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said to her, “Did you see the film yesterday?”
options: He asked her if she had seen the film the previous day.
He asked her if she saw the film yesterday.
He asked her did she see the film the previous day.
He asked her if he had seen the film the previous day.
questions.explanation: Rule: yes/no question uses 'if'; simple past becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day'; 'you' becomes 'she'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The judge said to the accused, “Why did you steal the money?”
options: The judge asked the accused why did he steal the money.
The judge asked the accused why he had stolen the money.
The judge asked the accused why he stole the money.
The judge asked the accused why you had stolen the money.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question takes statement order; simple past becomes past perfect; 'you' becomes 'he'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, “My brother will be coming here next week.”
options: She said that her brother will be coming here next week.
She said that my brother would be coming there the following week.
She said that her brother would be coming there the following week.
She said that her brother would come there the previous week.
questions.explanation: Rule: will be coming becomes would be coming; 'here' becomes 'there'; 'next week' becomes 'the following week'; 'my' becomes 'her'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Raju said to me, “I shall help you if you ask me.”
options: Raju told me that he would help me if you asked me.
Raju told me that he will help me if I ask him.
Raju told me that I would help him if I asked him.
Raju told me that he would help me if I asked him.
questions.explanation: Rule: shall becomes would and the present in the 'if' clause becomes past; 'I' becomes 'he', 'you' becomes 'I', 'me' becomes 'him'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Gopal said to Sita, “How did you reach here so early?”
options: Gopal asked Sita how she had reached there so early.
Gopal asked Sita how did she reach there so early.
Gopal asked Sita how she reached here so early.
Gopal asked Sita how he had reached there so early.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question takes statement order; simple past becomes past perfect; 'you' becomes 'she'; 'here' becomes 'there'.
questions.shortcut: Reporting verb in past: backshift the tense (am/is to was, will to would, V2 to had + V3); fix pronouns by speaker/listener; today/tomorrow/here become that day/next day/there.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I had finished my work before she came.”
options: He said that he had finished his work before she has come.
He said that he had finished his work before she came.
He said that he has finished his work before she came.
He said that I had finished my work before she came.
questions.explanation: Rule: past perfect cannot backshift further, so it stays 'had finished'; only the pronouns change (I becomes he, my becomes his).
